title: ‘MAGA Self-Immolated’: How EVERYTHING Fell Apart for Trump and Republicans This Year
author: Asawin Suebsaeng

On Tuesday night, [everything](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-groan-trump-
and-stephen) fell apart for U.S. President Donald Trump, his MAGA movement,
his administration, and his Republican Party.

The scale of the defeat, driven by a titanic backlash from voter groups and
grassroots blocs, and by Democratic enthusiasm and fury at the ruling party,
is hard to overstate. Trump and his people failed at effectively everything -
_EVERYTHING_ - they wanted to do, or forestall, in the U.S. midterms.

The "blue tsunami" - all over the country, in the Senate, in the House, at
governor's mansions, in Texas, Kansas, and other deep red, Trump-voting areas
- was [significantly grander](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-2026-bloodbath-
was-way) than even some of the biggest doomsayers in the Trumpland elite
predicted.

The authoritarian, woefully corrupt president's [attempts to rig
the](https://zeteo.com/p/19-ways-trump-and-republicans-are) [2026
elections](https://zeteo.com/p/inside-trumps-desperate-final-push) fell flat,
beaten back by [sustained voting-protection
efforts](https://zeteo.com/p/inside-dems-plans-to-fight-back-trump-ice-polls)
and the sheer size of the Democratic victories. The Republican Party's mission
to destroy Black voting power in the South [met with](https://slate.com/news-
and-politics/2026/11/black-voters-blue-wave-callais-gerrymander-
dummymander.html) a ferocious, record-shattering
"[Blacklash](https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2026/11/01/black-voters-
turnout-south-midterms-trump-01144574)." The gerrymander wars that President
Trump and conservatives started last year [blew
up](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/gerrymander-
dummymander-republicans-midterms-1235653320/) in their faces. Elon Musk's
mega-million-dollar spending, meant to rescue the GOP in a tough midterm
environment, was as helpful as many Trump advisers feared it would be,
mountains of cash unable to ["save" them](https://zeteo.com/p/elon-
musk-474-million).

The party unity that Trump and his fellow Republicans have been trying to
engineer crumbled almost as quickly as the results were called, with
conservative luminaries and former Trump rivals like Ted Cruz and Ron DeSantis
stepping out to distance themselves from a toxic, historically unpopular
presidency. (Good luck!) The campaigns of
_[extremely](https://zeteo.com/p/top-republicans-privately-admit-their)
_online __[hate](https://zeteo.com/p/why-was-ilhan-omars-home-raided-over),
[unalloyed bigotry](https://zeteo.com/p/what-about-arab-and-muslim-safety),
[abject cruelty, and in-your-face depravity](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-
warned-vivek-ramaswamy) - driven by Trump-endorsed nominees and in some cases
the White House itself - were forcefully rejected by U.S. voters, at times by
notably embarrassing margins for the MAGA-fied right. And the impressive 2024
gains among key groups that Trump and his allies had yearned to preserve,
particularly working-class and Hispanic voters, got torn to shreds, largely
because of anger over Trump's Iran war, his floundering economy, and his
relentless push to [terrorize
immigrants](https://www.tpr.org/2026-11-06/voters-rebuke-trump-
administrations-ice-raids-and-immigration-policies-at-the-polls) and
[ethnically cleanse the nation](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-springfield-
haitians-following-orders).

It was, and is, an unmitigated fiasco (to put it mildly) for Trump and his
demoralized coalition, if you can even call it that anymore. The vastness of
this event is something that numerous prominent political operatives, both on
the winning team and within the shaken ranks of institutionalized Trumpism,
tell **Zeteo** they're still in the middle of processing.
